provision: A monthly-paid wage is compared with the daily floor using the 365/12 factor, a daily-paid wage using the 393.5, 313/310 or 261/258 annual factors as the contract's paid rest days and holidays require.
reason: Probes authored 2026-09-30 (batch 9): paid rest days judge on 365 ÷ 12 — ₱21,139.59 pays (PH-WG59-1), ₱15,116.25 refuses (PH-WG59-2); a six-day roster judges on 313 ÷ 12 — ₱18,127.92 pays (PH-WG59-3), ₱15,116.25 refuses (PH-WG59-4). Unproven: the 365/12 monthly factor; 393.5, 313/310 and 258 annual factors. [LIT-01 2026-09-30] `work_rules.rate_conversions`: a daily wage's month is the Handbook factor (× 313 ÷ 12 on six days, × 261 ÷ 12 otherwise, as `ordinary_divisor_days`); a week × 52 ÷ 12 (SSS Circular 2014-002, as the engine cited); an hour × weekly hours × 52 ÷ 12 is the recorded default (law silent). Golden: tests/rate-conversions.test.ts, pending the test phase.
golden: Philippines — the DOLE daily-rate factors 365, 261 and 313
probe: PH-WG10-1; PH-WG24-1; PH-WG59-1; PH-WG59-2; PH-WG59-3; PH-WG59-4

golden: Philippines — a kasambahay is covered by SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG after one month of service (RA 10361 s.30)

provision: Wages are paid at least twice a month at intervals of no more than 16 days, in legal tender at or near the workplace, with receipts, and only lawful deductions (legal order, consent, loans) are made.
citation: Labor Code art.103 (original numbering); Omnibus Rules Book III Rule VIII s.3
reason: Re-judged 2026-09-30 against the probe cases. Proven: semi-monthly cadence with the month’s schemes in the first half (PH-HR03-1). Unproven: the 16-day interval check; legal tender, place and receipts; lawful-deduction authority, consent and priority. Recorded default (LIT-5, 2026-09-30): art.103 names no split day, only the 16-day interval; the semi-monthly halves are the 1st–15th and 16th–month end, paid on the 15th and the last day, so the longest interval is 16 days (15th to the 31st). A split before the 15th would leave a 17-day second half in a 31-day month.

provision: Hours worked include all time the employee is suffered or permitted to work; sixty minutes off for meals is owed and an untaken meal period is hours worked.
citation: PD 442 arts.84(b), 85 (E-Library text); DOLE Handbook 2024 ch.1 §§C–E
reason: Re-judged 2026-09-30 against the probe cases. Proven: the 60-minute meal break is not hours worked (PH-HR06-1, PH-WH09-1). Unproven: an untaken meal period counted as hours worked; waiting and training time.
golden: Philippines — a daily-paid employee’s hour is the day over eight, whatever the week (Handbook ch.2)

provision: A covered employee is paid for a regular holiday not worked if present or on paid leave on the preceding workday, and 200% of the day when it is worked; successive holidays and shutdowns follow the handbook rules.
citation: DOLE Handbook 2024 ch.2; Labor Code art.94 (original numbering)
reason: Probes authored 30 Sep 2026: an unworked regular holiday is paid when present on the preceding workday (PH-HR05-3) and unpaid after leave without pay on it, the Friday deciding for a Monday holiday (PH-HR05-2). Still unproven: successive holidays, shutdowns, preceding paid leave. Prior: Re-judged 2026-09-30 against the probe cases. Proven: a worked regular holiday at 200% (PH-HR05-1). Unproven: unworked regular holiday pay and the preceding-workday presence/paid-leave condition; successive holidays; shutdowns.
golden: PH audit 2026-01: a worked regular holiday is 200% of the day in all, a worked special day 130% (Handbook ch.2 §D, ch.3 §C, ch.4 §D)

provision: Overtime beyond eight hours earns +25% (+30% on rest/special/holiday days), rest-day and special-day work +30%, and night work 10:00 p.m.–6:00 a.m. a 10% differential; night hours are overtime-night only inside the day's last overtime hours.
citation: Labor Code arts.86, 87, 93, 94 (original numbering); DOLE Handbook 2024 ch.3–5
reason: Probes authored 30 Sep 2026: rest-day hours beyond eight at 169% (PH-HR06-2); overtime-night hour 10% of the overtime rate (PH-HR06-3). Still unproven: holiday overtime, ordinary night-shift differential. Prior: Re-judged 2026-09-30 against the probe cases. Proven: overtime +25% on an ordinary day (PH-HR06-1, PH-WH09-1); rest-day 130% (PH-HR06-1); special-day 130% (PH-HR05-1). Unproven: overtime +30% on rest, special and holiday days; night differential 10% and the overtime-night rule. [LIT-07 2026-09-30] Planned overtime and incentive hours are keyed in steps of `work_rules.overtime_unit_hours`: a write off the step is refused, a binding limit floors the approved hours to it, and clock hours past the plan below one step are not reported as UNPLANNED_OVERTIME. The law states no keying unit, so every PH version seeds 0.5, the recorded default (the engine's former built-in half hour, now configuration). Golden: tests/overtime-unit.test.ts, pending the test phase; no probe added.
golden: Philippines — a late start with no overtime earns the ordinary 10% night rate on its night hour (Labor Code art.86)

provision: Service charges collected by a covered establishment are distributed 100% to covered rank-and-file workers in equal shares at least twice a month.
reason: Merges PH-LB03 and shared tracker R17: no collected-pool, covered-worker, attendance, full-allocation and cadence mechanism; a precomputed allowance does not prove statutory distribution. DO 242-24 notice: https://dole.gov.ph/news/new-rules-on-service-charge-law-out/.

provision: An employee with a year of service gets five days' service incentive leave a year, convertible to cash at the salary rate on the date of commutation, pro rata, unless excluded.
citation: Labor Code art.95 (renumbered; original text lacks an SIL article); DOLE Handbook 2024 ch.7 §§A–D
reason: Re-judged 2026-09-30 against the probe cases. Proven: commutation of a given SIL quantity at the salary rate on exit (PH-HR15-1: 0.833 × 1,400 = 1,166.20). Unproven: derivation of the entitlement: the probe types the pro-rata 0.833 day as a leave_entries input (encash_days) rather than the engine deriving five days a year after a year of service pro rata (independent re-verification 30 Sep 2026); the one-year condition; the TASK_BASIS exclusion.
golden: Philippines — the statutory leave ladder on every version

provision: A pregnant covered female employee gets 105 days' maternity leave with full pay (60 for miscarriage or emergency termination; +15 for a qualified solo parent), continuous and uninterrupted, charged on calendar days; the leave does not depend on SSS registration age or paid contribution months.
reason: The 24 MATERNITY_LEAVE catalogue rows no longer gate on facts.SSS.since_months >= 3 (the three paid months in s.5(a) decide only the SSS cash benefit, PH-SS02); entitlement.calendar_days charges rest days; explicit EMERGENCY_TERMINATION event routes to 60 days (event input is free text). ph-maternity-entitlement probes approved a leave day with one month/no SSS registration and a 105-day span 5 Oct 2026–17 Jan 2027 as four cutoff entries retaining PHP20,000 gross; the later prewrite guard now refuses every approved unpinned maternity charge without a saved case allocation, so that BASIC expectation is no longer a valid settlement result and must be revised. Day 106+ needs a birth-matched benefit case whose solo_parent_documented qualification holds (event-valid solo-parent LGU document with its fact_evidence file): the catalogue's 120-day band reads event.case.facts.solo_parent_documented, not the employee's current flag (awaiting gate). Planner still accepts a standalone one-day entry. Open: seven-day caregiver allocation, holidays, adoptive parents (PH-HR51), live tenant and unusual pay bases; shared tracker R06. IRR: https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/96742.

Probe PH-HR12-1 fails (2026-09-29): the leave requires a certificate file and the production-path probe harness has no upload, so the entry is refused at input. 2026-09-30 (F04): the probe harness now uploads fixture files, asserts refusals, run warnings and company-scope charges; PH-HR12-1 attaches the VAWC certification as certificate_file; pending the probe run. provision: A woman with six months' aggregate service in the preceding twelve months gets up to two months' full-pay special leave after gynecological surgery.
reason: Phase 2, 2026-10-01: not configurable yet. The aggregate-service rule is employment.service_days_before(event.date, 12) >= 180, with 180 days as the owner-rule default because no six calendar months fall below it. But `service_periods`, the stints that function reads, is supplied only on the payroll path (gather.ts servicePeriods). The leave-entry eligibility context (src/lib/leave/context.ts personContext) passes none, so the function throws, and every surgery request would be refused. Configuring it would break the leave, so it stays a GAP for the leave context (owners D/E), not a seed fix. Prior: The current rule checks only continuous service, not aggregate service in the last twelve months (R24); overlap with maternity and medical evidence branches open.

provision: A rank-and-file employee who worked at least a month is paid a 13th month of one twelfth of the basic salary earned in the calendar year, not later than 24 December, and the employer reports compliance.
citation: PD 851 and Revised Guidelines; DOLE Handbook 2024 ch.13
reason: Phase 2, 2026-10-01, in all 22 unvoided versions: duty types THIRTEENTH_MONTH_PAYMENT (due 24 December) and THIRTEENTH_MONTH_DOLE_REPORT (due 15 January, completes with the DOLE reference); Duty instances are raised only by the daily obligation_calendar automation, and the probe harness reads `saved` rows before any automation runs, so no probe pins one yet (harness gap, owner H). Still unproven: at-least-one-month, rank-and-file limit, 24 December timing, compliance report. Prior: Re-judged 2026-09-30 against the probe cases. Proven: the one-twelfth rule on basic salary earned (leavers PH-HR15-1, PH-HR15-2, PH-HR16-1). Unproven: a full-year December 13th month; the at-least-one-month condition; the rank-and-file limit; the 24 December timing and compliance report.
golden: Philippines — 13th month pay keyed for December is a twelfth of the year’s basic, and the excess over ₱90,000 is withheld on

provision: An employee who resigns or is terminated before payment is owed the 13th month in proportion to time worked in the year, raised at off-boarding and paid in the final period.
citation: PD 851 Revised Guidelines ¶6 (DOLE Handbook 2024 ch.13 §G, §E); DOLE LA 06-20
reason: Re-judged 2026-09-30 against the probe cases. Proven: the pro-rata price one twelfth of the year’s basic earned (PH-HR15-1, PH-HR15-2, PH-HR16-1). Unproven: the raise at off-boarding: every probe types the THIRTEENTH_MONTH_PAY request itself (amount 0, priced by formula), so the SEPARATION raise is not exercised.
golden: Philippines — EM-1: off-boarding owes a June leaver the pro-rata 13th month, 180,000 ÷ 12 = 15,000

provision: Separation pay is one month per year on redundancy/labour-saving devices and half a month per year (at least one month) on retrenchment, closure or disease, a fraction of six months counting as a year; separation for causes beyond the employee's control is tax-exempt.
citation: PD 442 arts.283–284 (E-Library art.323; renumbered arts.298–299); NIRC s.32(B)(6)(b); DOLE Handbook 2024 ch.14
reason: Phase 2, 2026-10-01, in all 22 unvoided versions: duty type AUTHORISED_CAUSE_TERMINATION_NOTICE (EXIT with a recorded termination_cause, due one month before the last day, completes with the DOLE reference); Duty instances are raised only by the daily obligation_calendar automation, and the probe harness reads `saved` rows before any automation runs, so no probe pins one yet (harness gap, owner H). Prior: Re-judged 2026-09-30 against the probe cases. Proven: redundancy one month per year (PH-HR15-1); retrenchment half a month per year (PH-HR15-2); both outside withholding. Authored 30 Sep 2026, awaiting the test phase: a fraction of at least six months counts as a year (PH-HR15-3, 5 y 7 m → 6 × 15,225 = 91,350) and the one-month minimum (PH-HR15-4, 7 m → 30,450). Unproven: labour-saving devices; closure; disease (exit fact terminated_for_disease).
golden: Philippines — separation pay: a month per year on redundancy, half a month on retrenchment, closure or disease (Labor Code art.298–299)

provision: Absent a better plan, an employee retiring at 60–65 with at least five years' service gets at least half a month's salary (22.5 days) per year, six months counting as a year; underground/surface miners and race-horse jockeys have lower ages.
citation: RA 7641 (Labor Code art.302 renumbered); DOLE Handbook 2024 ch.15; RR 15-2025
reason: Re-judged 2026-09-30 against the probe cases. Proven: 22.5 days per year at 62 after ten years, tax-exempt (PH-HR16-1). Unproven: the five-year condition; a fraction of six months as a year; the 60–65 bounds; miners and jockeys.
golden: PH audit 2026-01: retirement pay is 22.5 days a year, six months counting a year; separation at the same seam

provision: A child worker may not work 8 p.m.–6 a.m. if under 15 or 10 p.m.–6 a.m. if 15–17; ages 15–17 are capped at 8 hours/day and 40/week; a work permit is required; where earnings are at least PHP200,000 a year the parent/guardian keeps at least 30% in trust with semi-annual accounting to DOLE.
reason: Phase 2, 2026-10-01, in all 22 unvoided versions: work limits minor_daily_hours (8 worked hours a day) and minor_weekly_hours (40 a week) for ages 15 to 17 (employee.age), judged at the roster gate.
